title: The Balance the Lines Record Standing to the Policyholder's Credit
content:
The balance the lines she submitted record standing to a policyholder's credit under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is set against what she is asked to send back. How much of that recorded balance is credited is settled as follows.

1. **Where the lines she submitted record her owing a balance and those days were not covered by this policy** — the whole of that recorded balance is set against what she sends back.
2. **Where the plan letter's own cost sharing would have left her a balance on those days** — only the part of the recorded balance above what the plan letter would have left is set against it.
3. **Where neither of those holds** — nothing is credited to her.

### The difference between the first two

The first case applies where the days in question were not covered by this policy at all. Nothing the plan letter provides was owing on those days, so the whole recorded balance is hers to be credited.

The second case allows for a balance the plan letter's own cost sharing would have left her in any event. What the plan letter would have left is measured on the amounts Medicare approved on those lines, as the part the plan letter does not cover. Only the recorded balance above that figure is credited, and where the recorded balance does not exceed it, nothing is credited.

### Hypothetical figures

Lines she submitted recording her owing 180.00 on days this policy did not cover: the whole 180.00 is credited to her.

Lines recording her owing 180.00 where the amounts Medicare approved come to 600.00 and the plan letter covers 100 per cent of the Part B coinsurance, so that its own cost sharing would have left her nothing: the whole 180.00 stands above what the plan letter would have left and is credited.

Lines recording her owing 180.00 where the plan letter would have left her 200.00: the recorded balance does not exceed what the plan letter would have left, and nothing is credited to her.
